node.title: Exact bignum evaluation at bounded scales: expansions unnecessary at candidates
node.statement: With N' <= ~400 absolute, the deciding class counts K are exactly computable big integers (binomial-sum sized ~2^400 at worst). At candidate points, EXACT K replaces the leading+second-order expansion entirely: the knife-edge condition sharpens from 'estimate cannot decide' to the exact Diophantine condition B* = floor(q/2^128) in [L, K), where L is the certified lower bound strength. (acl_second_order remains needed only for corridor WIDTH/candidate localization, not for tie decisions.)
node.notes: PROVED (my lane, exact computation, verifier green): exact table computed at all four rates; rate-1/2 shortfall 3.8 bits below gate; rate-1/4 gate in the staircase gap.
